clue.text: Author that's narrated The Beach?

indicators.note: narrated means spoken out, so the word for the beach is taken by its sound

parts.note: the beach is the shore

explanation.surface: A question about who voices the audiobook of a novel called The Beach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike. The question mark flags that the 'narrator' is a pun, not a reader of the book.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright and writer, so he is an author.

clue.text: Actress from Hair, with nothing on except new diamonds

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: except means leaving out, here dropping one letter from the word on

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An actress from the musical Hair appearing nude apart from a few diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on except new' is ON without its N, leaving O. Margaret Lockwood was a British film star of the 1930s-40s, and Lockwood is also the narrator of Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Lockwood was a leading British film star, so she is an example of an actress.

clue.text: Have courier deliver costumes

parts.note: to have something is to get it
UPS is a well-known parcel courier company

explanation.surface: Arranging for a delivery firm to bring some fancy-dress outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-ups are outfits, especially elaborate or odd costumes.

clue.text: Singer out to shake butt endlessly?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order, rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of butt is cut off

explanation.surface: A performer heading out on the dance floor to wiggle their behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims butt to BUT; 'out' rearranges SHAKE plus BUT. Kate Bush's first hit was Wuthering Heights, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Bush is an English singer-songwriter, best known for her 1978 hit Wuthering Heights.

clue.text: See 14
Sort of underwear, if cold in bed

indicators.note: in places the letter for cold inside the word for bed

parts.note: to bed someone is to lay them
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Choosing nightwear on the grounds of feeling chilly in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacy describes underwear trimmed with lace, so it names a kind of lingerie.

clue.text: Place to go if confused, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word for confused is taken by its sound

parts.note: to be thrown is to be confused or disconcerted

explanation.surface: Someone baffled about which way to head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to go' uses go in its slang sense of using the toilet, and throne is slang for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is a humorous slang word for the toilet, the place you go when you need to go.

clue.text: Out and about with bra off when Christ was born?

indicators.note: off suggests the word bra is disturbed, its letters jumbled

parts.note: Christ's birth is traditionally dated to year 0 AD, the start of the anno Domini count

explanation.surface: Someone going around town braless, cheekily framed as a nativity question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' jumbles BRA to ABR; the question mark covers treating the date of the Nativity as 0 AD, giving OAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad can mean out of doors and moving about, as rumours are abroad.

clue.text: Star Wars character aroused when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the last letter of the word for aroused round to the front

parts.note: to be woken is to be aroused; woke is its past tense

explanation.surface: A Star Wars figure who perks up when out on a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewoks are the small furry forest creatures of Return of the Jedi.

clue.text: Relative, one extremely lazy, as not having showered for ages?

definitions.text: as not having showered for ages?

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an means one, as in an apple

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of lazy

explanation.surface: A slovenly uncle who has not washed in a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in a dirty way, as someone unwashed for ages behaves or smells.

clue.text: One seeking votes regularly swears in tent?

parts.note: tents are made of canvas, and canvas is a word for a tent

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of swears, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A campaigner who keeps cursing while stuck inside a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes door to door soliciting support for a candidate.

clue.text: Go over clue type with no apparent answer

definitions.meaning: to go over a road is to traverse it

definitions.text: clue type with no apparent answer
definitions.meaning: a ...-reference clue such as 'See 14' shows no answer of its own

explanation.surface: A solver revising a kind of clue that seems to have no solution.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense refers to the cross-reference clues in this very grid, such as 5 down, which simply say 'See 14'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross is to go over; a cross-reference clue points elsewhere instead of having its own answer.

clue.text: Singer that's come with two females in place of Max

indicators.note: in place of says one set of letters replaces another inside the word for come

parts.note: come is slang for orgasm, a climax
taken as written, the letters to be replaced
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A singer arriving with two women instead of a man named Max.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer; with HEATH at 16 across he completes Heathcliff of Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard is a long-running British pop singer, known simply as Cliff.

clue.text: Want to keep womb, if not useless with ovaries removed?

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the word for want goes around the rest

parts.note: to want something is to need it

indicators.note: useless is read as us-less: the word for womb loses its letters U and S

parts.note: the womb is the uterus

explanation.surface: A medical musing about keeping a womb working after a spaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'useless' is split cheekily as us-less, a deletion signal, while also suggesting the uselessness of a sterilised animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutering a female animal means spaying it, which removes the ovaries.

clue.text: Bell on trilby with no rim seems ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests letters put into a silly new order
with no rim strips the outer letters off seems, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A bell perched on a brimless hat looks absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no rim' trims SEEMS to EEM; 'ridiculous' rearranges ON TRILBY plus EEM. Emily Bronte published Wuthering Heights as Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Bronte first published under the pen name Ellis Bell, so Bell is her pseudonym.

clue.text: Told a story in song

definitions.meaning: to tell a story can mean to fib, to say something untrue
a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: Someone who recounted a tale through singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lied is the past tense of fib, and also the German word for an art song.

clue.text: Johnny's no Southern bandleader

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a johnny is British slang for a condom, a sheath

explanation.surface: A remark that a man called Johnny is not a band leader from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath led a famous British big band; with CLIFF at 12 down he gives Heathcliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Heath was a celebrated British big-band leader of the 1940s and 50s.

clue.text: Person assisting with cleaning in hotel, supported by progressive group

indicators.note: in a down answer, being supported by means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ELP, Emerson Lake and Palmer, were a progressive rock band

explanation.surface: A cleaner working in a hotel, backed by a reforming organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive' looks political but points to prog rock: ELP, Emerson Lake and Palmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A home help is someone employed to do domestic chores for a person who needs assistance.

clue.text: Can Jack be sick?

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man called Jack is able to be sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun, slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for a prison, as in being in the can.

clue.text: Thirty days eating right soup with vegetables cut into strips

definitions.text: soup with vegetables cut into strips

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other

parts.note: June is one of the months with thirty days
a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A month spent eating soup with shredded vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Julienne describes thin matchstick strips of vegetables, and a clear soup made with them.

clue.text: Ring two daily papers frequently

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O
the FT, the Financial Times, and The Times are two British dailies

explanation.surface: Phoning a couple of newspapers often.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofttimes is an old-fashioned word meaning often.

clue.text: Singer that's leader of top hard rock group

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of top

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Rush were a Canadian rock band

explanation.surface: A lead singer fronting a hard-rock band at the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist. Thrushcross Grange is the Linton family home in Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: Silly person of note, lost in a city

parts.note: N is a note, short for note on music or banknote abbreviations

indicators.note: in places the letter for lost inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports results

explanation.surface: A notable fool who has got lost in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelly Dean is the housekeeper who narrates most of Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelly is British slang for a silly or effeminate person, as in a big girl's blouse.

clue.text: A couple of seconds away from getting undesired bug

indicators.note: away from means the letters are removed from the word that follows

parts.note: something needless is unwanted, not desired
S stands for second, so two seconds are SS

explanation.surface: Escaping an unwanted insect within a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect but is the verb to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate them, which is what to bug them means.

clue.text: Nightmare? That's an unknown quantity

definitions.meaning: a mare of the night: night is dark and a mare is a horse
someone whose abilities are not known

explanation.surface: A bad dream that turns out to be a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a contender of unknown ability, and a night mare is literally a dark horse.

clue.text: Church official writing article in study

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the room

parts.note: a den is a private study
a is the indefinite article used in writing

explanation.surface: A cleric writing a piece in his study.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior clergyman in charge of a cathedral or group of parishes.

clue.text: Deserve shows in the Arnolfini

indicators.note: shows in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painting that merits being displayed, like Van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: With SHAW at 1 down this makes Earnshaw, the family of Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to deserve, as in earning praise.

clue.text: Opening up, gets 12A

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: A doorway that, when raised, becomes something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, the cross of Christ, so it matches the answer to 12 across.

clue.text: Subordinate with flipping bum occupying 7

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembly round
occupying means sitting inside

parts.note: 7 across is a slang word for the toilet, also called a lav
ass is American slang for bottom, a bum

explanation.surface: A minion whose behind is sitting on the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath but is the reversal signal, applied after the insertion signalled by 'occupying'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal tenant owing allegiance, so a subordinate.

clue.text: Former president's heading off to see Kwesi Johnson?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Bill Clinton is a former US president

explanation.surface: An ex-president setting off to visit a reggae poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Linton Kwesi Johnson is a British dub poet, so the answer completes his name; Linton is also a family in Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name that goes before Kwesi Johnson, the Jamaican-British dub poet.
